title: Songbook and Harbor
premise: Quentin Okafor, a celebrated wedding planner who quietly stopped believing in marriage after her own engagement collapsed twenty years ago, joins an anonymous pen-pal program meant to pair strangers—only to discover her assigned correspondent is August Reyes, the rival planner whose firm has been poaching her clients and whose voice she has loathed at every industry gala. Bound by the program's rules of anonymity, they confess their fears, griefs, and buried dreams to each other while waging open war by day, until Quentin realizes the man she is falling for on paper is the enemy across the table. When a fire threatens the harborfront venue that holds both their futures, Quentin must choose between protecting her reputation and claiming a love that demands her whole heart; in the end, she plans one last wedding—her own—and signs her name to it.
about_author: Wendell Hartwell is a former harbor-town bookseller who spent a decade collecting other people's love letters before writing his own stories. He lives near the water, where he still answers letters by hand.

chapters.title: The Last Bouquet Toss
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. At a flawless wedding she orchestrated, Quentin watches the bride cry not with joy but with fear, and feels her old cynicism harden. Her assistant teases her about the anonymous pen-pal program she signed up for on a drunken dare. Beat: loneliness disguised as professionalism.

chapters.title: Rules of Correspondence
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. The program's coordinator explains the rules: no names, no photos, no meeting until both parties agree. Quentin writes her first letter, careful and guarded, telling herself it means nothing. Beat: cautious hope flickering under armor.

chapters.title: Enemy of the State of Matrimony
chapters.summary: August's POV. August Reyes, whose boutique firm just stole Quentin's biggest client, drafts his own first letter, venting about a rival he can't stop thinking about. He doesn't know his pen pal is that rival. Beat: irritation masking fascination.

chapters.title: Ink and Antagonism
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Their letters begin—polite, then pointed, as they argue about love without knowing it. By day, Quentin discovers August poached another client and declares war. Beat: dramatic irony tightening; readers see what they cannot.

chapters.title: What the Harbor Remembers
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Quentin visits the crumbling harborfront lighthouse hall her late mother once managed, now slated for demolition, and remembers why she became a planner: her mother believed weddings were promises kept in public. Beat: grief resurfacing as inheritance.

chapters.title: A Letter Too Honest
chapters.summary: August's POV. August admits in a letter that he sabotaged his own engagement years ago out of cowardice, and that he envies people who risk everything. Quentin reads it twice and writes back something true for the first time. Beat: walls cracking from both sides.

chapters.title: The Gala
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. At the industry gala, Quentin and August spar publicly over the harborfront contract while privately each wonders what their pen pal would say about the other. A near-miss: August almost mentions a detail only his correspondent knows. Beat: suspense of almost-discovery.

chapters.title: Small Safe Steps
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Quentin's ex-fiancé reappears, offering partnership and a comfortable, passionless reconciliation. She nearly says yes, then rereads her pen pal's last letter and declines. Beat: choosing the unknown over the safe.

chapters.title: Correspondence in Wartime
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. As their professional war escalates—leaked bids, stolen vendors—their letters grow tenderer, each apologizing for the day's cruelty in ink. Neither connects the timing. Beat: intimacy deepening against escalating conflict.

chapters.title: The Program's Fine Print
chapters.summary: August's POV. August learns the program pairs applicants by compatibility algorithm—and that his match's handwriting on an envelope looks achingly familiar. He begins testing Quentin with planted details. Beat: suspicion kindling into dread and longing.

chapters.title: Mother's Songbook
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Sorting her mother's things, Quentin finds a songbook of wedding hymns annotated with her parents' love story, including a song her mother promised would play at Quentin's wedding someday. Beat: inheritance reframed—not property, but permission to hope.

chapters.title: One Venue, Two Bids
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Both firms bid to restore the harborfront hall; the committee proposes a joint venture neither wants. Forced collaboration begins, all sharp words and accidental closeness. Beat: enemies chained together, chemistry igniting.

chapters.title: The Almost
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Working late in the half-restored hall, Quentin and August share a dance to test the acoustics and nearly kiss. She pulls away, terrified, and goes home to write her pen pal a letter she doesn't send. Beat: desire outrunning denial.

chapters.title: Confessions by Post
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Both write their most vulnerable letters yet—August confessing he may know who she is; Quentin confessing she's falling for someone impossible. Each misreads the other's confession as being about someone else. Beat: tragic misunderstanding at peak tension.

chapters.title: Discovery
chapters.summary: August's POV. August finds proof—her distinctive phrasing from a press interview matching a letter verbatim. His pen pal is Quentin. Reeling, he must decide whether to reveal it or let her end the correspondence on her own terms. Beat: knowledge as burden.

chapters.title: The Unmasking
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. At the hall's reopening preview, August reveals himself as her correspondent before the crowd. Humiliated and feeling manipulated, Quentin publicly tears up the joint contract and walks into the rain. Beat: climax of betrayal; love weaponized by timing.

chapters.title: Twenty Years of Small Steps
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Alone, Quentin confronts the truth: she hid behind anonymity because her whole life has been retreat since her broken engagement. Her mother's songbook falls open to the promise page. Beat: dark night of the soul turning toward choice.

chapters.title: The Fire
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. An electrical fire guts the restored hall days before its debut wedding. Quentin and August work side by side through the night salvaging what matters—her mother's songbook, his grandmother's rings used as decor. Beat: catastrophe burning away pretense.

chapters.title: Ashes and Vows
chapters.summary: August's POV. In the smoke-gray dawn, August tells Quentin the full truth of his engagement failure and asks nothing except the chance to be chosen knowingly this time. Quentin doesn't answer—but she doesn't leave. Beat: humility met with silence that isn't refusal.

chapters.title: Time Is Already Running Out
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. The program's final deadline arrives: correspondents must meet or be permanently unmatched. Quentin realizes August already chose her twice—on paper and in person—and that waiting for certainty is just fear in a nicer dress. Beat: decision crystallizing.

chapters.title: The Wedding Planner's Wedding
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. On the rebuilt harborfront deck, Quentin plans and executes her own wedding in forty-eight hours—imperfect, improvised, alive—with her mother's hymn sung as she walks down an aisle of salvaged wood. Beat: triumph; every theme resolved in action.

chapters.title: Songbook and Harbor
chapters.summary: Epilogue, alternating POV. One year later, their joint firm restores venues others abandon, and their letters continue anyway—now left on pillows and kitchen tables. Quentin adds a new page to the songbook for whoever inherits it next. Beat: peace; love as ongoing practice, not arrival.
